rounds.learn: An f-string is a string with an f in front of the quotes. Inside it, a name in curly braces gets swapped for its value.
rounds.task: Put your name in a variable. Then say hi to it with an f-string.
rounds.say: %out%. The {name} got swapped for what name holds.

rounds.learn: You can put math inside the braces too. Python works out the answer first, then drops it in.
rounds.task: You have 3 tools. Print that, then print how many you will have after you buy one more.
rounds.code:
tools = 3
print([[f]]"I have {tools} tools")
print(f"next week: [[{tools + 1}]]")
rounds.say: 3, then 4. The braces did the math for you.

rounds.task: Make city hold Paris. Print I live in Paris, using an f-string.
rounds.say: %out%. One f, one pair of braces.

rounds.task: Make item hold drill and price hold 40. Print exactly: drill costs 40 dollars
rounds.hint: item = "drill" and price = 40. Then print(f"{item} costs {price} dollars").

checks.msg: I need exactly: drill costs 40 dollars
Use an f-string, with f right before the quote.
Let the braces fill in price for you.

rounds.say: %out%. Two names, one sentence, zero gluing.
